brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

cover:0,0,0;full;top as dial face with prop:3 pencil and prop:4 pen lying on it as two hands at different angles, both visible from above

requirements.evidence: no motor, movement, pivot or rotating joint exists in catalog; props are static staging and cannot rotate or be driven
static props only suggest a fixed time; nothing keeps or tracks real time

finish.summary: Built a wall-hangable hex dial with two static pointer props suggesting hands. No moving clock mechanism exists in Hex Cluster parts or props, so turning hands and real timekeeping are unmet.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
